title.zh: 卷八十八 列傳第四十八 薛安都 沈文秀 崔道固
title.en: Volume 88 Biographies 48: Xue Andou, Shen Wenxiu, Cui Daogu
title.raw: 卷八十八 列傳第四十八 薛安都 沈文秀 崔道固 Volume 88 Biographies 48: Xue Andou, Shen Wenxiu, Cui Daogu

sentences.zh: 列傳第四十八 薛安都 沈文秀 崔道固

translations.literal: Biography 48: Xue Andou, Shen Wenxiu, Cui Daogu
translations.idiomatic: Biography 48: Xue Andou, Shen Wenxiu, and Cui Daogu

sentences.zh: 薛安都，河東汾陰人也。

translations.literal: Xue Andou was a native of Fenyin in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Andou was from Fenyin in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 世為強族，同姓有三千家。

translations.literal: For generations his clan had been powerful; those sharing his surname numbered three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: His family had been a powerful clan for generations, with three thousand households bearing the same surname.

sentences.zh: 父廣，為宗豪，高祖定關、河，以為上黨太守。

translations.literal: His father Guang was a local powerful figure; when the High Ancestor pacified Guan and He, he appointed him Governor of Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Guang was a local magnate. When Emperor Gaozu secured the Guan and He regions, he made him Governor of Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 安都少以勇聞，身長七尺八寸，便弓馬。

translations.literal: Andou was known from youth for bravery; he stood seven chi eight cun tall and was skilled with bow and horse.
translations.idiomatic: Andou won fame early for his courage. He stood seven foot eight in height and was expert with bow and horse.

sentences.zh: 索虜使助秦州刺史北賀汨擊反胡白龍子，滅之。

translations.literal: The northern barbarians sent him to assist the Governor of Qinzhou Bei He'ni in attacking the rebellious Hu BAI Longzi and destroyed him.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei sent him to aid Qinzhou Governor Bei He'ni in crushing the rebel Hu leader BAI Longzi.

sentences.zh: 由是為偽雍、秦二州都統，州各有刺史，都統總其事。

translations.literal: Thereby he became Commander-in-chief of the two pseudo-prefectures Yong and Qin; each prefecture had its own governor, and the commander-in-chief oversaw all their affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made supreme commander over the puppet Yong and Qin prefectures, each of which still had its own governor while he held overall authority.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十一年，索虜主拓跋燾擊芮芮大敗，安都與宗人薛永宗起義，永宗營汾曲，安都襲得弘農。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Yuanjia, when the Wei ruler Tuoba Tao suffered a great defeat attacking the Rouran, Andou and his clansman Xue Yongzong rose in revolt—Yongzong encamped along the Fen bend while Andou seized Hongnong by surprise.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year of Yuanjia, when the Wei ruler Tuoba Tao was routed by the Rouran, Andou and his kinsman Xue Yongzong rose in rebellion. Yongzong encamped along the Fen bend while Andou seized Hongnong in a surprise attack.

sentences.zh: 會北地人蓋吳起兵，遂連衡相應。

translations.literal: At the same time Gai Wu of Beidi raised troops, and they joined forces in mutual support.
translations.idiomatic: When Gai Wu of Beidi also took up arms, the rebel forces linked up in mutual support.

sentences.zh: 燾自率眾擊永宗，滅其族，進擊蓋吳。

translations.literal: Tao himself led troops to attack Yongzong, exterminated his clan, and then advanced against Gai Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Tao personally led his army against Yongzong, wiped out his clan, and then marched on Gai Wu.

sentences.zh: 安都料眾寡不敵，率壯士辛靈度等，棄弘農歸國。

translations.literal: Andou judged that he was outmatched; leading stalwarts such as Xin Lingdu, he abandoned Hongnong and returned to the Song court.
translations.idiomatic: Judging the odds impossible, Andou led stalwarts including Xin Lingdu, abandoned Hongnong, and submitted to the Song.

sentences.zh: 太祖延見之，求北還構扇河、陝，招聚義眾。

translations.literal: The Taizu received him in audience; he requested to return north to stir up rebellion along the Yellow River and in Shaanxi and gather loyal forces.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu received him and approved his plan to go back north to stir rebellion along the Yellow River and in Shaanxi and rally loyalists.

sentences.zh: 上許之，給錦百匹，雜繒三百匹。

translations.literal: The emperor consented and granted him a hundred bolts of brocade and three hundred bolts of miscellaneous silks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and gave him a hundred bolts of brocade and three hundred bolts of assorted silks.

sentences.zh: 復襲弘農，虜已增戍，城不可克，蓋吳又死，乃退還上洛。

translations.literal: He again attacked Hongnong, but the barbarians had reinforced the garrison and the city could not be taken; Gai Wu had also died, so he withdrew to Shangluo.
translations.idiomatic: He struck at Hongnong again, but the barbarians had reinforced the garrison and the city would not fall. After Gai Wu died as well, he withdrew to Shangluo.

sentences.zh: 世祖鎮襄陽，板為揚武將軍、北弘農太守。

translations.literal: When the Shizu was stationed at Xiangyang, Andou was appointed General Who Displays Martial Might and Governor of Northern Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu held Xiangyang, Andou was commissioned General Who Displays Martial Might and Governor of Northern Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 虜漸強盛，安都乃歸襄陽。

translations.literal: As the barbarians grew ever stronger, Andou returned to Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: As the barbarians grew stronger, Andou returned to Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 從叔沈亦同歸國，官至綏遠將軍、新野太守。

translations.literal: His cousin Shen likewise submitted to the Song and rose to General Who Pacifies the Distance and Governor of Xinye.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Shen returned with him and eventually reached the rank of General Who Pacifies the Distance and Governor of Xinye.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，隨王誕版安都為建武將軍，隨柳元景向關、陝，率步騎居前，所向克捷，事在元景傳。

translations.literal: In year twenty-seven the Prince of Suiwang Dan appointed Andou General Who Establishes Martial Power; he marched with Liu Yuanjing toward Guan and Shaanxi at the head of infantry and cavalry, winning wherever he went—the account is in Yuanjing's biography.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-seven Prince Dan of Sui appointed Andou General Who Establishes Martial Power. Andou marched with Liu Yuanjing toward Guan and Shaanxi at the head of the army and won every engagement—the full account is in Yuanjing's biography.

sentences.zh: 軍還，誕版為後軍行參軍。

translations.literal: When the army returned, Dan commissioned him Aide-de-Camp of the Rear Army.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaign Dan appointed him Aide-de-Camp of the Rear Army.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，除始興王濬征北行參軍，加建武將軍。

translations.literal: In year twenty-nine he was made Aide-de-Camp on the Northern Campaign of Prince of Shixing Jun, with the added title General Who Establishes Martial Power.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-nine he was appointed Aide-de-Camp on the Northern Campaign of Prince Jun of Shixing, with the additional rank of General Who Establishes Martial Power.

sentences.zh: 魯爽向虎牢，安都復隨元景北出，即據關城，期俱濟河取蒲阪。

translations.literal: When Lu Shuang advanced on Hulao, Andou again followed Yuanjing north, seized the pass city, and planned to cross the river together to take Puban.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Shuang moved on Hulao, Andou again went north with Yuanjing, seized the pass city, and planned to ford the river together and take Puban.

sentences.zh: 會爽退，安都復率所領隨元景引還。

translations.literal: When Shuang withdrew, Andou again led his command back with Yuanjing.
translations.idiomatic: When Shuang retreated, Andou again led his troops back with Yuanjing.

sentences.zh: 仍伐西陽五水蠻。

translations.literal: He then campaigned against the Wushui Man of Xiyang.
translations.idiomatic: He then campaigned against the Wushui barbarians of Xiyang.

sentences.zh: 世祖伐逆，轉參軍事，加寧朔將軍，領馬軍，與柳元景俱發。

translations.literal: When the Shizu marched to suppress the rebellion, Andou was transferred to staff duty, made General Who Pacifies the North, and placed in command of the horse troops, setting out with Liu Yuanjing.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu marched to suppress the usurpation, Andou was transferred to staff duty, made General Who Pacifies the North, and given command of the cavalry, setting out with Liu Yuanjing.

sentences.zh: 四月十四日，至朱雀航，橫矛瞋目，叱賊將皇甫安民等曰：「賊弑君父，何心事之！

translations.literal: On the fourteenth day of the fourth month they reached the Zhuque ford. Andou levelled his spear, glared, and shouted at the rebel generals Huangfu Anmin and others: "You serve men who murdered their lord and father—how can you face them?"
translations.idiomatic: On the fourteenth day of the fourth month they reached the Zhuque ford. Andou levelled his spear, glared, and shouted at the rebel generals Huangfu Anmin and the rest: "You serve men who murdered their lord and father—how can you bear to follow them?"

sentences.zh: 」世祖踐阼，除右軍將軍。

translations.literal: The Shizu took the throne and appointed him General of the Right Army.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu ascended the throne and appointed him General of the Right Army.

sentences.zh: 五月四日，率所領騎為前鋒，直入殿庭。

translations.literal: On the fourth day of the fifth month he led his cavalry as vanguard straight into the palace hall.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth day of the fifth month he led his cavalry as vanguard straight into the palace courtyard.

sentences.zh: 賊尚有數百人，一時奔散。

translations.literal: Several hundred rebels remained; they fled all at once.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred rebels were still there; they scattered at once.

sentences.zh: 以功封南鄉縣男，食邑五百戶。

translations.literal: For his merit he was enfeoffed as Baron of Nanxiang with an estate of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was enfeoffed as Baron of Nanxiang with a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 安都從征關、陝，至臼口，夢仰頭視天，正見天門開，謂左右曰：「汝見天門開不？

translations.literal: On campaign in Guan and Shaanxi, Andou reached Jiukou and dreamed that he looked up and saw the Heavenly Gate open. He asked his attendants, "Do you see the Heavenly Gate opening?"
translations.idiomatic: On campaign in Guan and Shaanxi, Andou reached Jiukou and dreamed that he looked up and saw the Heavenly Gate standing open. He asked those beside him, "Do you see the Heavenly Gate open?"

sentences.zh: 」至是歎曰：「夢天開，乃中興之象邪！」

translations.literal: At this he sighed and said, "To dream the heavens open—is that not an omen of dynastic renewal!"
translations.idiomatic: At this he sighed and said, "To dream the heavens open—is that not a sign of renewal for the dynasty!"

sentences.zh: 從弟道生，亦以軍功為大司馬參軍。

translations.literal: His younger cousin Daosheng likewise won office through military merit as Aide to the Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: His younger cousin Daosheng also won rank through military merit as Aide to the Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 犯罪，為秣陵令庾淑之所鞭。

translations.literal: Daosheng committed an offence and was flogged by Moling Magistrate Yu Shuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Daosheng broke the law and was flogged by Moling Magistrate Yu Shuzhi.

sentences.zh: 安都大怒，乃乘馬從數十人，令左右執矟，欲往殺淑之。

translations.literal: Andou flew into a rage, mounted his horse with several dozen followers, had his attendants take up spears, and set out to kill Shuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Andou was furious. He mounted his horse with several dozen men, ordered his attendants to take up spears, and set out to kill Shuzhi.

sentences.zh: 行至朱雀航，逢柳元景。

translations.literal: On the way he reached the Zhuque ford and met Liu Yuanjing.
translations.idiomatic: On the road he reached the Zhuque ford and met Liu Yuanjing.

sentences.zh: 元景遙問：「薛公何處去？

translations.literal: Yuanjing called from afar, "Lord Xue, where are you bound?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing called from a distance, "Lord Xue, where are you going?"

sentences.zh: 」安都躍馬至車後曰：「小子庾淑之鞭我從弟，今詣往刺殺之。

translations.literal: Andou spurred up behind the carriage and said, "That whelp Yu Shuzhi flogged my cousin—I am on my way to stab him to death."
translations.idiomatic: Andou spurred up behind the carriage and said, "That whelp Yu Shuzhi flogged my cousin. I am on my way to stab him to death."

sentences.zh: 」元景慮其不可駐，乃紿之曰：「小子無宜適，卿往與手，甚快。

translations.literal: Fearing he could not be halted, Yuanjing deceived him: "The lad does not deserve to live. Go give him a beating yourself—it will feel wonderful."
translations.idiomatic: Fearing he could not be stopped, Yuanjing deceived him: "The lad deserves no better. Go beat him yourself—you will feel much better."

sentences.zh: 」安都既回馬，復追呼之：「別宜與卿有所論。

translations.literal: Andou had already turned his horse when Yuanjing called him back again: "Wait—I have something else to discuss with you."
translations.idiomatic: Andou had already turned his horse when Yuanjing called him back: "Wait—I have something else to say to you."

sentences.zh: 」令下馬入車。

translations.literal: He ordered Andou to dismount and enter the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: He told Andou to dismount and get into the carriage.

sentences.zh: 既入車，因責讓之曰：「卿從弟服章言論，與寒細不異，雖復人士，庾淑之亦何由得知？

translations.literal: Once inside he reproved him: "Your cousin's dress and speech are no different from those of humble commoners; even if he were a gentleman, how was Yu Shuzhi to know?"
translations.idiomatic: Once inside he reproved him: "Your cousin's dress and speech are no different from a commoner's. Even if he were a gentleman, how was Yu Shuzhi to know?"

sentences.zh: 且人身犯罪，理應加罰，卿為朝廷勳臣，宜崇奉法憲，云何放恣，輒欲於都邑殺人？

translations.literal: Besides, when a man commits a crime punishment is proper. You are a meritorious servant of the court and ought to uphold the law—why give free rein to yourself and try to kill someone in the capital?"
translations.idiomatic: Besides, when a man commits a crime he ought to be punished. You are a meritorious servant of the court and should uphold the law—why indulge yourself and try to kill someone in the capital?"

sentences.zh: 非唯科律所不容，主上亦無辭以相宥。

translations.literal: This is forbidden not only by statute; the sovereign would have no grounds to excuse you.
translations.idiomatic: That is forbidden not only by law; the sovereign would have no grounds to pardon you.

sentences.zh: 」因載之俱歸，安都乃止。

translations.literal: He took Andou back with him in the carriage, and Andou desisted.
translations.idiomatic: He took Andou back with him in the carriage, and Andou stopped.

sentences.zh: 其年，以憚直免官。

translations.literal: That year he was dismissed from office for his bluntness.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was removed from office for his outspokenness.

sentences.zh: 孝建元年，復除左軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiaojian he was reappointed General of the Left Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xiaojian he was again appointed General of the Left Army.

sentences.zh: 二月，魯爽反叛，遣安都及冗從僕射胡子反、龍驤將軍宗越率步騎據歷陽。

translations.literal: In the second month, when Lu Shuang rebelled, the emperor sent Andou together with Supernumerary Attendant Hu Zifan and General of the Soaring Dragon Zong Yue with infantry and cavalry to hold Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, when Lu Shuang rebelled, the court sent Andou with Supernumerary Attendant Hu Zifan and General of the Soaring Dragon Zong Yue to hold Liyang with infantry and cavalry.

sentences.zh: 爽遣將鄭德玄戍大峴，德玄使前鋒楊胡與輕兵向歷陽。

translations.literal: Shuang sent his general Zheng Dexuan to garrison Great Xian; Dexuan sent his vanguard Yang Hu with light troops toward Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang sent his general Zheng Dexuan to garrison Great Xian. Dexuan sent his vanguard Yang Hu with light troops toward Liyang.

sentences.zh: 安都遣宗越及歷陽太守程天祚逆擊破之，斬胡與及其軍副。

translations.literal: Andou sent Zong Yue and Liyang Governor Cheng Tianzuo to intercept and defeat them, beheading Hu Yu and his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Andou sent Zong Yue and Liyang Governor Cheng Tianzuo to meet and defeat them, beheading Hu Yu and his deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 德玄復使其司馬梁嚴屯峴東，安都幢主周文恭晨往偵候，因而襲之，悉禽；

translations.literal: Dexuan again sent his marshal Liang Yan to camp east of the pass. Andou's banner commander Zhou Wengong went out at dawn to reconnoitre and then raided them, capturing all;
translations.idiomatic: Dexuan again sent his marshal Liang Yan to camp east of the pass. Andou's banner commander Zhou Wengong went out at dawn to scout and then raided them, capturing them all;

sentences.zh: 賊未敢進。

translations.literal: The rebels did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels dared not advance.

sentences.zh: 世祖詔安都留三百人守歷陽，渡還採石，遷輔國將軍、竟陵內史。

translations.literal: The Shizu ordered Andou to leave three hundred men guarding Liyang, cross back to Caishi, and promoted him to General Who Assists the State and Internal Administrator of Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu ordered Andou to leave three hundred men at Liyang, cross back to Caishi, and promoted him to General Who Assists the State and Internal Administrator of Jingling.

sentences.zh: 四月，魯爽使弟瑜率三千人出小峴，爽尋以大眾阻大峴。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Lu Shuang sent his younger brother Yu with three thousand men out through Little Xian, while Shuang himself soon blocked Great Xian with his main force.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Lu Shuang sent his younger brother Yu with three thousand men through Little Xian, while Shuang himself soon blocked Great Xian with his main army.

sentences.zh: 又遣安都步騎八千度江，與歷陽太守張幼緒等討爽。

translations.literal: Andou was again sent with eight thousand infantry and cavalry across the river, together with Liyang Governor Zhang Youxu and others, to attack Shuang.
translations.idiomatic: Andou was sent again with eight thousand infantry and cavalry across the river, together with Liyang Governor Zhang Youxu and others, to attack Shuang.

sentences.zh: 安都軍副建武將軍譚金率數十騎挑戰，斬其偏帥。

translations.literal: Andou's deputy, General Who Establishes Martial Power Tan Jin, led several dozen horsemen to challenge battle and cut down an enemy flank commander.
translations.idiomatic: Andou's deputy Tan Jin, General Who Establishes Martial Power, led several dozen horsemen to challenge battle and cut down an enemy flank commander.

sentences.zh: 幼緒恇怯，輒引軍退還，安都復還歷陽。

translations.literal: Youxu was cowardly and at once withdrew his army; Andou returned again to Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Youxu was timid and at once pulled his army back; Andou returned again to Liyang.

sentences.zh: 臧質久不至，世祖復遣沈慶之濟江督統諸軍。

translations.literal: Zang Zhi was long in coming. The Shizu again sent Shen Qingzhi across the river to take overall command of the armies.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Zhi was slow to arrive. Emperor Xiaowu again sent Shen Qingzhi across the river to take overall command of the armies.

sentences.zh: 爽軍食少，引退，慶之使安都率輕騎追之；

translations.literal: Shuang's army was short of provisions and withdrew. Qingzhi had Andou lead light cavalry in pursuit;
translations.idiomatic: Shuang's army was short of food and withdrew. Qingzhi had Andou lead light cavalry in pursuit;

sentences.zh: 四月丙戌，及爽於小峴，爽自與腹心壯騎繼後。

translations.literal: On the day bingxu of the fourth month they caught Shuang at Little Xian; Shuang himself followed at the rear with his trusted crack horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingxu of the fourth month they caught Shuang at Little Xian. Shuang himself followed at the rear with his trusted crack horsemen.

sentences.zh: 譚金先薄之，不能入，安都望見爽，便躍馬大呼，直往刺之，應手而倒，左右範雙斬爽首。

translations.literal: Tan Jin closed first but could not break in. Andou saw Shuang, spurred forward with a great shout, ran straight at him and thrust—Shuang fell at the stroke, and his attendant Fan Shuang cut off Shuang's head.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Jin closed first but could not break through. Andou saw Shuang, spurred forward with a great shout, ran straight at him and thrust—Shuang fell at the blow, and his attendant Fan Shuang cut off Shuang's head.

sentences.zh: 爽累世梟猛，生習戰陳，咸云萬人敵。

translations.literal: Shuang's family had been fierce for generations; he had fought from birth and all called him a match for ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang's family had been fierce for generations; he had known battle from birth, and all said he was a match for ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 安都單騎直入，斬之而反，時人皆云關羽之斬顏良，不是過也。

translations.literal: Andou charged in alone on horseback, killed him, and returned. People said even Guan Yu's slaying of Yan Liang was no better.
translations.idiomatic: Andou charged in alone on horseback, killed him, and returned. People said even Guan Yu's slaying of Yan Liang was no greater feat.

sentences.zh: 進爵為侯，增邑五百戶，并前千戶。

translations.literal: He was advanced to marquis, his fief increased by five hundred households to one thousand in all.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to marquis, his fief increased by five hundred households to one thousand in all.

sentences.zh: 時王玄謨距南郡王義宣、臧質於梁山，安都復領騎為支軍。

translations.literal: When Wang Xuamo held Yishuan and Zang Zhi of the Prince of Nan command at Liangshan, Andou again commanded cavalry as a supporting army.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Xuamo held the Prince of Nan command Yishuan and Zang Zhi at Liangshan, Andou again commanded cavalry as a supporting force.

sentences.zh: 賊有水步營在蕪湖，安都遣將呂興壽率數十騎襲之，賊眾驚亂，斬首及赴水死者甚眾。

translations.literal: The rebels had river and land camps at Wuhu. Andou sent his officer Lu Xingshou with several dozen horsemen to raid them; the enemy panicked and many were beheaded or drowned.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had river and land camps at Wuhu. Andou sent his officer Lu Xingshou with several dozen horsemen to raid them; the enemy panicked, and many were beheaded or drowned.

sentences.zh: 義宣遣將劉湛之及質攻玄謨，玄謨命眾軍擊之，使安都引騎出賊陣右。

translations.literal: Yishuan sent Liu Zhanzhi and Zhi to attack Xuamo. Xuamo ordered the armies to strike and had Andou lead cavalry out to the enemy's right flank.
translations.idiomatic: Yishuan sent Liu Zhanzhi and Zhi to attack Xuamo. Xuamo ordered the armies to strike and had Andou lead cavalry out to the enemy's right.

sentences.zh: 譚金三歷賊陳，乘其隙縱騎突之，諸將係進。

translations.literal: Tan Jin crossed the enemy formation three times, seized an opening to charge with his horsemen, and the other generals pressed in behind.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Jin crossed the enemy formation three times, seized a gap to charge with his horsemen, and the other generals followed in support.

sentences.zh: 是朝，賊馬軍發蕪湖，欲來會戰，望安都騎甚盛，隱山不敢出。

translations.literal: That morning the rebel horse troops set out from Wuhu intending to join battle, but seeing Andou's cavalry in great strength they hid in the hills and did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: That morning the rebel cavalry set out from Wuhu intending to join battle, but seeing Andou's horsemen in great strength they hid in the hills and did not emerge.

sentences.zh: 賊陣東南猶堅，安都橫擊陷之，賊遂大潰。

translations.literal: The enemy's southeast wing was still firm; Andou struck across and broke it, and the rebels collapsed utterly.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy's southeast wing was still holding; Andou struck across and broke it, and the rebels collapsed completely.

sentences.zh: 安都隊主劉元儒於艦中斬湛之首。

translations.literal: Andou's squad leader Liu Yuanru cut off Zhan's head aboard a ship.
translations.idiomatic: Andou's squad leader Liu Yuanru cut off Zhan's head on board a ship.

sentences.zh: 轉太子左衛率。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Leader of the Crown Prince's Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Leader of the Crown Prince's Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 大明元年，虜向無鹽，東平太守劉胡出戰失利。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daming the barbarians advanced on Wuyan; Dongping Governor Liu Hu fought and was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Daming the barbarians advanced on Wuyan. Dongping Governor Liu Hu fought and was defeated.

sentences.zh: 二月，遣安都領馬軍北討，東陽太守沈法系水軍向彭城，並受徐州刺史申坦節度。

translations.literal: In the second month Andou was sent north at the head of the horse troops; Dongyang Governor Shen Faxing led the river force toward Pengcheng; both were under the command of Xuzhou Inspector Shen Tan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Andou was sent north at the head of the cavalry; Dongyang Governor Shen Faxing led the river force toward Pengcheng. Both were under Xuzhou Inspector Shen Tan.

sentences.zh: 上戒之曰：「賊若可及，便盡力殄之。

translations.literal: The emperor warned them: "If the enemy can still be overtaken, destroy them with all your strength."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor warned them: "If the enemy can still be caught, destroy them with all your strength."

sentences.zh: 若度已回，可過河耀威而反。

translations.literal: If they have already turned back across the Yellow River, you may cross to display your might and return."
translations.idiomatic: If they have already crossed back north, you may cross the river to show your might and return."

sentences.zh: 」時虜已去，坦求回軍討任榛，見許。

translations.literal: The barbarians had already gone. Tan requested to turn the army to attack the Ren bandits and was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians had already withdrawn. Tan asked to turn the army against the Ren bandits and was permitted.

sentences.zh: 安都當向左城，左城去滑臺二百餘里，安都以去虜鎮近，軍少不宜分行。

translations.literal: Andou was to proceed toward Zuocheng, more than two hundred li from Huatai. Andou held that since they were close to the barbarian garrison and their force was small, they should not divide.
translations.idiomatic: Andou was to move on Zuocheng, more than two hundred li from Huatai. Andou argued that with the barbarian garrison so near and their army so small, they should not split their forces.

sentences.zh: 至東坊城，遇任榛三騎，討擒其一，餘兩騎得走。

translations.literal: At Dongfangcheng they met three Ren bandit horsemen, captured one in pursuit, and the other two escaped.
translations.idiomatic: At Dongfangcheng they met three Ren bandit horsemen, captured one in the pursuit, and the other two got away.

sentences.zh: 任榛聞知，皆得逃散。

translations.literal: On hearing of this, all the Ren bandits fled and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ren bandits heard, they all fled and scattered.

sentences.zh: 時天旱，水泉多竭，人馬疲困，不能遠追。

translations.literal: There was drought; springs dried up; men and horses were worn out and could not pursue far.
translations.idiomatic: There was drought and the springs ran dry; men and horses were exhausted and could not pursue far.

sentences.zh: 安都、法系並白衣領職，坦繫尚方。

translations.literal: Andou and Faxing both retained their posts in plain dress; Tan was imprisoned in the Imperial Workshops.
translations.idiomatic: Andou and Faxing both retained their posts in plain dress as punishment; Tan was imprisoned in the Imperial Workshops.

sentences.zh: 任榛大抵在任城界，積世逋叛所聚，所在皆棘榛深密，難為用師，故能久自保藏，屢為民患。

translations.literal: The Ren bandits lay mostly within Rencheng territory—a refuge for long-accumulated fugitives. Everywhere thornbrakes ran deep and dense, so troops could not be used effectively; thus they long preserved themselves and repeatedly harried the people.
translations.idiomatic: The Ren bandits lay mostly within Rencheng—a gathering place for long-accumulated fugitives. Everywhere the thorn scrub ran deep and dense, so armies could not operate effectively; thus they long preserved themselves and repeatedly plagued the people.

sentences.zh: 安都明年復職，改封武昌縣侯，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: The next year Andou was restored to office, refiefed as Marquis of Wuchang, and made Regular Attendant at the Imperial Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Andou was restored to office, refiefed as Marquis of Wuchang, and made Regular Attendant at the Imperial Gate.

sentences.zh: 七年，又加征虜將軍，為太子左衛率十年，終世祖世不轉。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was again made General Who Subdues the Barbarians. He remained Leader of the Crown Prince's Left Guard for ten years and was never transferred through the rest of the Shizu reign.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was again made General Who Subdues the Barbarians. He remained Leader of the Crown Prince's Left Guard for ten years and was never transferred through the rest of Emperor Xiaowu's reign.

sentences.zh: 泰始二年正月，索兒、光世竝在省，安都信催令速去，二人俱自省逃出，攜安都諸子及家累，席捲北奔。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Taishi, Suo'er and Guangshi were both at court. Trusting urgent messages telling him to leave quickly, Andou sent them—and both fled from court, taking Andou's sons and dependents and sweeping north in flight.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year of Taishi, Suo'er and Guangshi were both at court. Trusting urgent word to leave quickly, Andou urged them on—and both fled from court, taking Andou's sons and household and sweeping north in flight.

sentences.zh: 青州刺史沈文秀、冀州刺史崔道固並皆同反。

translations.literal: Qingzhou Inspector Shen Wenxiu and Jizhou Inspector Cui Daogu both rebelled as well.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhou Inspector Shen Wenxiu and Jizhou Inspector Cui Daogu rebelled as well.

sentences.zh: 文秀遣劉彌之、張靈慶、崔僧琁三軍，道固遣子景征、傅靈越領眾，並應安都。

translations.literal: Wenxiu sent the three armies of Liu Mizhi, Zhang Lingqing, and Cui Sengqin; Daogu sent his son Jingzheng and Fu Lingyue with troops—all to join Andou.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu sent the three armies of Liu Mizhi, Zhang Lingqing, and Cui Sengqin; Daogu sent his son Jingzheng and Fu Lingyue with troops—all to support Andou.

sentences.zh: 彌之等南出下邳，靈越自泰山道向彭城。

translations.literal: Mizhi and the others went south from Xiapi; Lingyue took the Mount Tai route toward Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Mizhi and the others marched south from Xiapi; Lingyue took the Mount Tai route toward Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 時濟陰太守申闡據睢陵城起義，索兒率靈越等攻之。

translations.literal: Jiyin Governor Shen Chan then raised the standard of loyalty at Suiling. Suo'er led Lingyue and others to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyin Governor Shen Chan had raised the standard of loyalty at Suiling. Suo'er led Lingyue and others to attack him.

sentences.zh: 安都使同黨裴祖隆守下邳城，彌之等至下邳，改計歸順，因進軍攻祖隆，僧琁不同，率所領歸安都。

translations.literal: Andou had his associate Pei Zulong hold Xiapi. When Mizhi and the others reached Xiapi they changed plans and submitted, then advanced to attack Zulong; Sengqin disagreed and led his force back to Andou.
translations.idiomatic: Andou had his associate Pei Zulong hold Xiapi. When Mizhi and the others reached Xiapi they changed plans and submitted, then advanced to attack Zulong. Sengqin disagreed and led his troops back to Andou.

sentences.zh: 索兒聞彌之有異志，舍睢陵馳赴下邳，彌之等未戰潰散，竝為索兒所執，見殺。

translations.literal: Suo'er heard Mizhi was wavering, abandoned Suiling and raced to Xiapi. Mizhi's men collapsed without fighting and were all seized and killed by Suo'er.
translations.idiomatic: Suo'er heard Mizhi was wavering, abandoned Suiling, and raced to Xiapi. Mizhi's men collapsed without fighting and were all seized and killed by Suo'er.

sentences.zh: 時太宗以申令孫為徐州，代安都。

translations.literal: The Taizong made Shen Lingsun Inspector of Xuzhou in place of Andou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming made Shen Lingsun Inspector of Xuzhou in place of Andou.

sentences.zh: 令孫進據淮陽，密有反志，遣人告索兒曰：「欲相從順，而百口在都。

translations.literal: Lingsun advanced and held Huaiyang, secretly harboring rebellious intent, and sent word to Suo'er: "I wish to join you in submission, but my whole household is in the capital."
translations.idiomatic: Lingsun advanced and held Huaiyang, secretly harboring rebellious intent, and sent word to Suo'er: "I wish to join you, but my whole household is in the capital."

sentences.zh: 可進軍見攻，若戰敗被執，家人可得免禍。

translations.literal: Advance and attack me openly. If I am defeated and captured, my family may be spared."
translations.idiomatic: Come advance and attack me openly. If I am defeated and captured, my family may be spared."

sentences.zh: 」索兒乃遣靈越向淮陽，令孫出城，為相距之形，既而奔散，北投索兒。

translations.literal: Suo'er then sent Lingyue toward Huaiyang. Lingsun came out of the city as though to oppose him, then scattered his men and fled north to join Suo'er.
translations.idiomatic: Suo'er then sent Lingyue toward Huaiyang. Lingsun came out as if to oppose him, then scattered his troops and fled north to Suo'er.

sentences.zh: 索兒使令孫說闡令降，闡既降，索兒執闡及令孫，並殺之。

translations.literal: Suo'er had Lingsun persuade Chan to surrender; once Chan had submitted, Suo'er seized Chan and Lingsun and killed them both.
translations.idiomatic: Suo'er had Lingsun persuade Chan to surrender. Once Chan had submitted, Suo'er seized Chan and Lingsun and killed them both.

sentences.zh: 索兒因引軍渡淮，軍糧不給，掠奔百姓穀食。

translations.literal: Suo'er then led his army across the Huai. With no army rations, they plundered fleeing commoners for grain.
translations.idiomatic: Suo'er then crossed the Huai with his army. With no rations, they plundered fleeing commoners for grain.

sentences.zh: 太宗遣齊王率前將軍張永、寧朔將軍垣山寶、王寬、員外散騎侍郎張寘震、蕭順之、龍驤將軍張季和、黃文玉等諸軍北討。

translations.literal: The Taizong sent the Prince of Qi at the head of Former General Zhang Yong, General Who Pacifies the North Yuan Shanbao, Wang Kuan, Supernumerary Gentleman-at-Large Zhang Zhenzhen, Xiao Shunzhi, General of the Soaring Dragon Zhang Jihe, Huang Wenyu, and other armies northward.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming sent the Prince of Qi at the head of Former General Zhang Yong, General Who Pacifies the North Yuan Shanbao, Wang Kuan, Supernumerary Gentleman-at-Large Zhang Zhenzhen, Xiao Shunzhi, General of the Soaring Dragon Zhang Jihe, Huang Wenyu, and other armies northward.

sentences.zh: 其年五月，軍次平原，索兒等率馬步五千，列陳距戰，擊大破之。

translations.literal: That fifth month the army halted at Pingyuan. Suo'er and the others led five thousand horse and foot, drew up in battle, and were smashed.
translations.idiomatic: That fifth month the army halted at Pingyuan. Suo'er and the others led five thousand horse and foot, drew up in battle array, and were utterly defeated.

sentences.zh: 索兒又虜掠民穀，固守石樑，齊王又率鎮北參軍趙曇之、呂湛之擊之。

translations.literal: Suo'er plundered civilian grain again and held Stone Bridge. The Prince of Qi again led Northern Campaign Aides Zhao Tanzhi and Lu Zhenzhi to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Suo'er plundered civilian grain again and held firm at Stone Bridge. The Prince of Qi again led Northern Campaign Aides Zhao Tanzhi and Lu Zhenzhi to attack them.

sentences.zh: 索兒軍無資實，所資野掠，既見攻逼，無以自守，於是奔散；

translations.literal: Suo'er's army had no real supplies and lived on plunder from the countryside; pressed by attack, they could not hold and fled in disorder;
translations.idiomatic: Suo'er's army had no real supplies and lived on countryside plunder. Under attack they could not hold and broke and fled;

sentences.zh: 又追破之於葛家白鵠。

translations.literal: They were again pursued and defeated at Gejia Baihe.
translations.idiomatic: They were pursued and defeated again at Gejia Baihe.

sentences.zh: 索兒走向樂平縣界，為申令孫子孝叔所斬。

translations.literal: Suo'er fled toward the border of Leping county and was beheaded by Shen Lingsun's son Xiaoshu.
translations.idiomatic: Suo'er fled toward Leping county and was beheaded by Shen Lingsun's son Xiaoshu.

sentences.zh: 安都子道智、大將范雙走向合肥，詣南汝陰太守裴季降。

translations.literal: Andou's son Daozhi and his great general Fan Shuang fled toward Hefei and submitted to Southern Runan Governor Pei Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Andou's son Daozhi and his great general Fan Shuang fled to Hefei and surrendered to Southern Runan Governor Pei Ji.

sentences.zh: 時武衛將軍王廣之領軍隸劉勔，攻殷琰於壽陽。

translations.literal: At that time Martial Guard General Wang Guangzhi led troops under Liu Xu and attacked Yin Yan at Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Martial Guard General Wang Guangzhi led troops under Liu Xu in the attack on Yin Yan at Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 傅靈越奔逃，為廣之軍人所生禽，厲聲曰：「我傅靈越也。

translations.literal: Fu Lingyue fled and was captured alive by Guangzhi's soldiers. He shouted loudly, "I am Fu Lingyue.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Lingyue fled and was captured alive by Guangzhi's men. He shouted, "I am Fu Lingyue.

sentences.zh: 汝得賊何不即殺？

translations.literal: You have caught a rebel—why do you not kill me at once?"
translations.idiomatic: You have caught a rebel—why not kill me at once?"

sentences.zh: 」生送詣勔，勔躬自慰勞，詰其叛逆。

translations.literal: They took him alive to Xu, who personally comforted and questioned him about his rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: They took him alive to Xu, who personally comforted him and questioned him about his rebellion.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「九州唱義，豈獨在我。

translations.literal: He answered, "The whole realm rose in righteous revolt—how could it be mine alone?"
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "The whole realm rose in righteous revolt—how could the fault be mine alone?"

sentences.zh: 」勔又問：「四方阻逆，無戰不禽，主上皆加以曠蕩，即其才用。

translations.literal: Xu asked again, "Rebels everywhere have been blocked and, battle after battle, captured; the sovereign has shown great clemency and employed each man according to his talent.
translations.idiomatic: Xu asked again, "Rebels everywhere have been blocked and captured in battle after battle; the sovereign has shown great clemency and employed each according to his talent.

sentences.zh: 卿何不早歸天闕，乃逃命草間乎？

translations.literal: Why did you not return early to the imperial court, but flee for your life among the weeds?"
translations.idiomatic: Why did you not return early to the imperial court instead of fleeing for your life among the weeds?"

sentences.zh: 」靈越答曰：「薛公舉兵淮北，威震天下，不能專任智勇，委付子侄，致敗之由，實在於此。

translations.literal: Lingyue answered, "Lord Xue raised arms north of the Huai, his might shaking the realm, yet he could not rely solely on wisdom and courage but entrusted affairs to sons and nephews—the reason for defeat lies in this.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyue replied, "Lord Xue raised arms north of the Huai and his might shook the realm, yet he could not rely on wisdom and courage alone but entrusted command to sons and nephews—the root of defeat lies here."

sentences.zh: 然事之始末，備皆參豫，人生歸於一死，實無面求活。

translations.literal: Yet from first to last I took part in everything. A man's life ends in death; I truly have no face left to beg for life."
translations.idiomatic: Yet I took part from beginning to end. A man's life ends in death; I have no face left to beg for life."

sentences.zh: 」勔壯其意，送還京師。

translations.literal: Xu admired his spirit and sent him back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Xu admired his bearing and sent him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 太宗欲加原宥，靈越辭對如一，終不回改，乃殺之。

translations.literal: The Taizong wished to pardon him, but Lingyue answered as before and would not change; he was therefore executed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming wished to pardon him, but Lingyue answered as before and would not change; he was therefore executed.

sentences.zh: 靈越，清河人也。

translations.literal: Lingyue was a native of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyue was from Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 時輔國將軍、山陽內史程天祚據郡同安都，攻圍彌時，然後歸順。

translations.literal: At that time General Who Assists the State and Internal Administrator of Shanyang Cheng Tianzuo held his commandery with Andou; after a long siege he finally submitted.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Cheng Tianzuo, General Who Assists the State and Internal Administrator of Shanyang, had held his commandery with Andou; after a long siege he submitted.

sentences.zh: 子勛平定，安都遣別駕從事史畢眾愛、下邳太守王煥等奉啟書詣太宗歸款，曰：「臣庸隸荒萌，偷生上國，過蒙世祖孝武皇帝過常之恩，犬馬有心，實感恩遇。

translations.literal: After Zixun was pacified, Andou sent his Registrar Bi Zhong'ai, Xiapi Governor Wang Huan, and others with a memorial to the Taizong offering submission, saying, "Your servant, a crude man from the borderlands, stole life in the upper kingdom and received beyond measure the exceptional grace of Emperor Xiaowu; this dog and horse has a heart and is truly grateful for the favor shown.
translations.idiomatic: After Zixun was pacified, Andou sent his Registrar Bi Zhong'ai, Xiapi Governor Wang Huan, and others with a memorial to Emperor Ming offering submission, saying, "Your servant, a crude man from the borderlands, stole life in the upper kingdom and received beyond measure the exceptional grace of Emperor Xiaowu; this dog and horse has a heart and is truly grateful for the favor shown.

sentences.zh: 是以晉安始唱，投誠孤往，不期生榮，實存死報。

translations.literal: Therefore when the Prince of Jin'an first raised the call, I offered my loyalty alone and unaided, not expecting glory in life but intending to repay with death."
translations.idiomatic: So when the Prince of Jin'an first raised the call, I went alone in loyalty, not hoping for glory in life but ready to repay with death."

sentences.zh: 今天命大歸，群迷改屬，輒率領所部，束骸待誅，違拒之罪，伏聽湯鑊。

translations.literal: "Now that Heaven's mandate has returned, the deluded have changed allegiance, I lead my command, bind my body and await execution, and for the crime of resistance submit to the boiling cauldron."
translations.idiomatic: "Now that Heaven's mandate has returned and the deluded have changed allegiance, I lead my command, bind my body and await execution, and for the crime of resistance submit to the boiling cauldron."

sentences.zh: 」索兒之死也，安都使柳光世守下邳，至是亦率所領歸降。

translations.literal: When Suo'er died, Andou had Liu Guangshi hold Xiapi; he too now led his command in submission.
translations.idiomatic: After Suo'er's death Andou had Liu Guangshi hold Xiapi; he now led his troops in submission as well.

sentences.zh: 太宗以四方已平，欲示威於淮外，遣張永、沈攸之以重軍迎之。

translations.literal: The Taizong, with the four quarters already pacified, wished to display might beyond the Huai and sent Zhang Yong and Shen Youzhi with a heavy army to receive Andou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming, with the four quarters already pacified, wished to display might beyond the Huai and sent Zhang Yong and Shen Youzhi with a heavy army to receive Andou.

sentences.zh: 安都謂既已歸順，不應遣重兵，懼不免罪，乃遣信要引索虜。

translations.literal: Andou thought that since he had already submitted, a heavy army should not have been sent; fearing he would not escape punishment, he sent messages inviting the northern barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Andou thought that since he had already submitted, a heavy army should not have been sent. Fearing he would not escape punishment, he sent messages inviting the northern barbarians.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，索虜遣博陵公尉遲苟人、城陽公孔伯恭二萬騎救之。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year the barbarians sent the Duke of Boling Yuanchi Gouren and the Duke of Chengyang Kong Bogong with twenty thousand horsemen to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year the barbarians sent the Duke of Boling Yuanchi Gouren and the Duke of Chengyang Kong Bogong with twenty thousand horsemen to his aid.

sentences.zh: 永等引退，安都開門納虜，虜即授安都徐州刺史、河東公。

translations.literal: Yong and the others withdrew; Andou opened the gates and admitted the barbarians, who at once appointed him Inspector of Xuzhou and Duke of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Yong withdrew; Andou opened the gates to the barbarians, who immediately made him Inspector of Xuzhou and Duke of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 四年三月，召還桑乾。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourth year he was summoned back to Sanggan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fourth year he was recalled to Sanggan.

sentences.zh: 五年，死於虜中，時年六十。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he died among the barbarians, aged sixty.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he died in barbarian lands, aged sixty.

sentences.zh: 初，安都起兵，長史蘭陵儼密欲圖之，見殺。

translations.literal: When Andou first raised troops, his Chief Clerk Yan of Lanling secretly plotted against him and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Andou first took up arms, his Chief Clerk Yan of Lanling plotted against him in secret and was put to death.

sentences.zh: 安都未向桑乾，前軍將軍裴祖隆謀殺苟人，舉彭城歸順，事泄，見誅。

translations.literal: Before Andou went to Sanggan, Vanguard General Pei Zulong plotted to kill Gouren and surrender Pengcheng; the plot was exposed and he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Before Andou went to Sanggan, Vanguard General Pei Zulong plotted to kill Gouren and hand Pengcheng over to the Song; the plot leaked and he was executed.

sentences.zh: 員外散騎侍郎孫耿之擊索兒戰死，及劉彌之、張靈慶皆戰敗見殺，並為太宗所哀，追贈儼光祿勳，祖隆寧朔將軍、兗州刺史，耿之羽林監，彌之輔國將軍、青州刺史，靈慶寧朔將軍、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: Supernumerary Gentleman-at-Large Sun Gengzhi died fighting Suo'er; Liu Mizhi, Zhang Lingqing, and others were defeated and killed in battle—all were mourned by the Taizong, who posthumously enfeoffed Yan as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Zulong as General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Yanzhou, Gengzhi as Inspector of the Feathered Forest, Mizhi as General Who Assists the State and Inspector of Qingzhou, and Lingqing as General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Supernumerary Gentleman-at-Large Sun Gengzhi died fighting Suo'er; Liu Mizhi, Zhang Lingqing, and others were defeated and killed in battle—all were mourned by Emperor Ming, who posthumously enfeoffed Yan as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Zulong as General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Yanzhou, Gengzhi as Inspector of the Feathered Forest, Mizhi as General Who Assists the State and Inspector of Qingzhou, and Lingqing as General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 安都子伯令、環龍，亡命梁、雍二州之間。

translations.literal: Andou's sons Boling and Huanlong were outlaws between Liang and Yong provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Andou's sons Boling and Huanlong lived as outlaws between Liang and Yong.

sentences.zh: 三年，率亡命數千人襲廣平，執太守劉冥虯，攻順陽，克之，略有義成、扶風，置立守宰。

translations.literal: In the third year they led several thousand outlaws to raid Guangping, seized Governor Liu Mingjiao, attacked Shunyang and took it, and overran parts of Yicheng and Fufeng, setting up local officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year they led several thousand outlaws against Guangping, seized Governor Liu Mingjiao, took Shunyang by assault, overran parts of Yicheng and Fufeng, and set up local officials.

sentences.zh: 雍州刺史巴陵王休若遣南陽太守張敬兒、新野太守劉攘兵擊破之，並禽。

translations.literal: Yongzhou Inspector the Prince of Baling Xiuruo sent Nanyang Governor Zhang Jing'er and Xinye Governor Liu Rangbing to defeat them and capture them both.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhou Inspector Prince Xiuruo of Baling sent Nanyang Governor Zhang Jing'er and Xinye Governor Liu Rangbing to defeat them and take them both captive.

sentences.zh: 先是，東安、東莞二郡太守張讜守團城，在彭城東北。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhang Chan, Governor of Dong'an and Dongguan, held Tuancheng northeast of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhang Chan, Governor of Dong'an and Dongguan, had held Tuancheng northeast of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 始同安都，末亦歸順，太宗以為東徐州刺史，復為虜所沒。

translations.literal: He first joined Andou but in the end also submitted; the Taizong made him Inspector of Eastern Xuzhou, but the territory was again lost to the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: He first joined Andou but in the end also submitted; Emperor Ming made him Inspector of Eastern Xuzhou, but the territory was again lost to the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 景和元年，遷督青州之東莞、東安二郡諸軍事、建威將軍、青州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jinghe he was transferred to Commander over military affairs in Dongguan and Dong'an of Qingzhou, General Who Establishes Martial Power, and Inspector of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jinghe he was made Commander over military affairs in Dongguan and Dong'an of Qingzhou, General Who Establishes Martial Power, and Inspector of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 時帝狂悖無道，內外憂危，文秀將之鎮，部曲出屯白下，說慶之曰：「主上狂暴如此，土崩將至，而一門受其寵任，萬物皆謂與之同心。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor was mad and lawless; within and without all were in peril. As Wenxiu was about to take up his post, his troops encamped at Baixia and he said to Qingzhi, "The sovereign is violent and reckless to this degree; the realm is about to collapse. Yet our whole house enjoys his special favor, and everyone believes we are of one mind with him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then mad and lawless and peril threatened within and without. As Wenxiu was about to take up his post his troops encamped at Baixia, and he told Qingzhi, "The sovereign is violent to this degree; the realm is about to collapse. Yet our whole house enjoys his special favor, and everyone thinks we are of one mind with him.

sentences.zh: 且此人性情無常，猜忌特甚，將來之禍，事又難測。

translations.literal: Moreover this man's nature is inconstant and his suspicion extreme; the calamity to come will be hard to foresee.
translations.idiomatic: And this man's nature is inconstant and his suspicion extreme—the coming calamity will be hard to foresee.

sentences.zh: 今因此眾力，圖之易於反掌，千載一時，萬不可失。

translations.literal: Now, with this force, to plot against him would be easier than turning one's hand—a chance that comes once in a thousand years and must not be lost."
translations.idiomatic: With the force we have now, to strike at him would be easier than turning one's hand—a chance that comes once in a thousand years and must not be lost."

sentences.zh: 」慶之不從。

translations.literal: Qingzhi would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi refused.

sentences.zh: 文秀固請非一，言輒流涕，終不回。

translations.literal: Wenxiu pressed again and again, speaking with tears each time, but in the end could not turn him.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu pleaded again and again, weeping as he spoke, but could not move him in the end.

sentences.zh: 文秀既行，慶之果為帝所殺。

translations.literal: After Wenxiu had departed, Qingzhi was indeed killed by the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: After Wenxiu had left, Qingzhi was indeed killed by the emperor.

sentences.zh: 慶之死後，帝遣直閣江方興領兵誅文秀，方興未至，太宗已定亂，馳驛駐之。

translations.literal: After Qingzhi's death the emperor sent Palace Attendant Jiang Fangxing with troops to execute Wenxiu. Before Fangxing arrived, the Taizong had already settled the turmoil and sent a fast courier to halt him.
translations.idiomatic: After Qingzhi's death the emperor sent Palace Attendant Jiang Fangxing with troops to execute Wenxiu. Before Fangxing arrived, Emperor Ming had already settled the turmoil and sent a fast courier to halt him.

sentences.zh: 方興既至，為文秀所執。

translations.literal: When Fangxing arrived he was seized by Wenxiu.
translations.idiomatic: Fangxing arrived and was seized by Wenxiu.

sentences.zh: 尋見釋，遣還京師。

translations.literal: He was soon released and sent back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was released soon after and sent back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 時晉安王子勛據尋陽反叛，六師外討，徵兵於文秀。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Jin'an Zixun held Xunyang in rebellion and the six armies campaigned abroad; troops were levied from Wenxiu.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin'an Zixun then held Xunyang in rebellion while the six armies campaigned abroad, and troops were levied from Wenxiu.

sentences.zh: 文秀遣劉彌之、張靈慶、崔僧琁三軍赴朝廷。

translations.literal: Wenxiu sent the three armies of Liu Mizhi, Zhang Lingqing, and Cui Sengqin to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu sent the three armies of Liu Mizhi, Zhang Lingqing, and Cui Sengqin to serve the court.

sentences.zh: 時徐州刺史薛安都已同子勛，遣使報文秀，以四方齊舉，勸令同逆，文秀即令彌之等回應安都。

translations.literal: At that time Xuzhou Inspector Xue Andou had already joined Zixun and sent messengers urging Wenxiu, saying the four quarters had all risen and urging him to rebel together; Wenxiu at once ordered Mizhi and the others to respond to Andou.
translations.idiomatic: Xuzhou Inspector Xue Andou had already joined Zixun and sent word urging Wenxiu on, saying the four quarters had all risen; Wenxiu at once ordered Mizhi and the others to answer Andou.

sentences.zh: 彌之等尋歸順，事在安都傳。

translations.literal: Mizhi and the others soon submitted—the account is in Andou's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Mizhi and the others soon came over—the account is in Andou's biography.

sentences.zh: 彌之青州強姓，門族甚多，諸宗從相合率奔北海，據城以拒文秀。

translations.literal: Mizhi was of a powerful Qingzhou clan with many kinsmen; the clansmen combined and fled to Beihai, holding the city against Wenxiu.
translations.idiomatic: Mizhi belonged to a powerful Qingzhou clan with many kinsmen; the clansmen banded together, fled to Beihai, and held the city against Wenxiu.

sentences.zh: 平原、樂安二郡太守王玄默據琅邪，清河、廣川二郡太守王玄邈據盤陽城，高陽、勃海二郡太守劉乘民據臨濟城，並起義。

translations.literal: Pingyuan and Le'an Governor Wang Xuanmo held Langye; Qinghe and Guangchuan Governor Wang Xuanmiao held Panyang; Gaoyang and Bohai Governor Liu Chenmin held Linji—all rose in loyal revolt.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuanmo, Governor of Pingyuan and Le'an, held Langye; Wang Xuanmiao of Qinghe and Guangchuan held Panyang; Liu Chenmin of Gaoyang and Bohai held Linji—all rose in loyal revolt.

sentences.zh: 文秀司馬房文慶謀應之，為文秀所殺。

translations.literal: Wenxiu's marshal Fang Wenqing plotted to join them and was killed by Wenxiu.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu's marshal Fang Wenqing plotted to join them and Wenxiu had him killed.

sentences.zh: 文秀遣軍主解彥士攻北海陷之，乘民從弟伯宗合率鄉兵，復克北海，因率所領向青州所治東陽城。

translations.literal: Wenxiu sent Commander Xie Yanshi to attack Beihai and take it. Chenmin's cousin Bozong combined with local militia, retook Beihai, and then led his force toward Dongyang, the seat of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu sent Commander Xie Yanshi to attack and take Beihai. Chenmin's cousin Bozong rallied local militia, retook Beihai, and marched on Dongyang, the seat of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 文秀拒之，伯宗戰敗被創，弟天愛扶持將去，伯宗曰：「丈夫當死戰場，以身殉國，安能歸死兒女手中乎！

translations.literal: Wenxiu resisted him. Bozong was defeated and wounded; his younger brother Tian'ai supported him as he was about to leave. Bozong said, "A man should die on the battlefield, giving his body for the state—how can he return to die in the hands of women and children!
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu resisted him. Bozong was beaten and wounded; his brother Tian'ai helped him as he was about to withdraw. Bozong said, "A man should die on the battlefield for the state—how can he go home to die in the hands of women and children!

sentences.zh: 弟可速去，無為兩亡。

translations.literal: Brother, go quickly—do not let us both perish."
translations.idiomatic: Brother, go at once—do not let us both die."

sentences.zh: 」乃見殺，追贈龍驤將軍、長廣太守。

translations.literal: He was then killed and posthumously made General of the Soaring Dragon and Governor of Changguang.
translations.idiomatic: He was killed and posthumously made General of the Soaring Dragon and Governor of Changguang.

sentences.zh: 太宗遣青州刺史明僧皓、東莞、東安二郡太守李靈謙率軍伐文秀。

translations.literal: The Taizong sent Qingzhou Inspector Ming Senghao and Dongguan and Dong'an Governor Li Lingqian with armies against Wenxiu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming sent Qingzhou Inspector Ming Senghao and Dongguan and Dong'an Governor Li Lingqian with armies against Wenxiu.

sentences.zh: 玄邈、乘民、僧皓等並進軍攻城，每戰輒為文秀所破，離而復合，如此者十餘。

translations.literal: Xuanmiao, Chenmin, Senghao, and the others all advanced to besiege the cities; each battle was defeated by Wenxiu, yet they drew off and came together again—more than ten times in this way.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanmiao, Chenmin, Senghao, and the rest all advanced to besiege the cities; Wenxiu defeated them in every battle, yet they withdrew and gathered again—more than ten times over.

sentences.zh: 泰始二年八月，尋陽平定，太宗遣尚書度支郎崔元孫慰勞諸義軍，隨僧皓戰敗見殺，追贈寧朔將軍、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the second year of Taishi Xunyang was pacified. The Taizong sent Minister of Revenue Cui Yuansun to comfort the loyalist armies; he was defeated in battle with Senghao and killed, and posthumously made General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the second year of Taishi Xunyang was pacified. Emperor Ming sent Minister of Revenue Cui Yuansun to comfort the loyalist armies; he was defeated in battle with Senghao and killed, and posthumously made General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 上遣文秀弟文炳詔文秀曰：「皇帝前問督青州、徐州之東莞、東安二郡諸軍事、建威將軍、青州刺史，朕去歲撥亂，功振普天，於卿一門，特有殊澤，卿得延命至今，誰之力邪？

translations.literal: The court sent Wenxiu's younger brother Wenbing with an edict to Wenxiu, saying, "The emperor inquires of the Commander over military affairs in Dongguan and Dong'an of Qingzhou, General Who Establishes Martial Power, and Inspector of Qingzhou: I put down disorder last year and my merit shook the whole realm; to your house alone I showed special grace. You have lived until now—whose power is that?
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Wenxiu's younger brother Wenbing with an edict saying, "The emperor asks the Commander over military affairs in Dongguan and Dong'an of Qingzhou, General Who Establishes Martial Power, and Inspector of Qingzhou: I put down disorder last year and my merit shook the realm; to your house alone I showed special grace. You have lived until now—by whose power?

sentences.zh: 何故背國負恩，遠同逆豎。

translations.literal: Why then betray the state and fail in gratitude, joining the rebels from afar?
translations.idiomatic: Why betray the state and fail in gratitude, joining rebels from afar?

sentences.zh: 今天下已定，四方寧一，卿獨守窮城，何所歸奉？

translations.literal: Now the realm is settled and the four quarters at peace—why do you alone hold this desperate city, and to whom will you offer allegiance?
translations.idiomatic: The realm is settled and the four quarters at peace—why do you alone hold this desperate city, and to whom will you turn?

sentences.zh: 且卿百口在都，兼有墳墓，想情非木石，猶或顧懷。

translations.literal: Moreover your whole household is in the capital, and you have ancestral graves as well; you are not wood or stone—surely you still have some regard.
translations.idiomatic: Your whole household is in the capital and you have ancestral graves besides; you are not wood or stone—surely something still moves you.

sentences.zh: 故指遣文炳具相宣示。

translations.literal: Therefore I have sent Wenbing to make all this clear to you.
translations.idiomatic: I have therefore sent Wenbing to lay all this before you.

sentences.zh: 凡諸逆郎，親為戎首，一不加罪，文炳所具。

translations.literal: As for all the other rebels, though they led the armies in person, not one was punished—the particulars are in Wenbing's report.
translations.idiomatic: All the other rebel leaders, though they commanded armies in person, were punished not at all—the details are in Wenbing's report.

sentences.zh: 卿獨何人，而能自立。

translations.literal: Who are you alone, that you can stand apart?
translations.idiomatic: Who are you, to stand alone?

sentences.zh: 便可速率部曲，同到軍門，別詔有司，一無所問。

translations.literal: You may at once lead your command to the army gate; a separate edict will instruct the officials to question you about nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Lead your command at once to the army gate; a separate edict will tell the officials to question you about nothing.

sentences.zh: 如其不爾，國有常刑，非惟戮及弟息，亦當夷卿墳壟，既以謝齊土百姓，亦以勞將士之心。

translations.literal: If you do not, the state has its regular punishments—not only your sons and brothers will be executed, but your ancestral graves will also be destroyed, both to answer to the people of Qi and to satisfy the hearts of the armies.
translations.idiomatic: If you refuse, the state has its regular punishments—not only your sons and brothers will die, but your ancestral graves will be destroyed as well, both to answer the people of Qi and to satisfy the armies.

sentences.zh: 故有今詔。

translations.literal: Therefore this edict."
translations.idiomatic: Hence this edict."

sentences.zh: 」三年二月，文秀歸命請罪，即安本任。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year Wenxiu submitted and asked pardon, and was confirmed in his original post.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the third year Wenxiu submitted and begged pardon, and kept his original post.

sentences.zh: 先是，冀州刺史崔道固亦據歷城同逆，為土人起義所攻，與文秀俱遣信引虜；

translations.literal: Earlier Jizhou Inspector Cui Daogu had also held Licheng in rebellion with the rebels and was attacked by local loyalists; like Wenxiu he sent messages inviting the barbarians;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Jizhou Inspector Cui Daogu had also held Licheng with the rebels and was attacked by local loyalists; like Wenxiu he too sent for the barbarians;

sentences.zh: 虜遣將慕輿白曜率大眾援之，文秀已受朝命，乃乘虜無備，縱兵掩擊，殺傷甚多。

translations.literal: The barbarians sent General Murong Baiyao with a great army to aid them. Wenxiu had already received the court's commission and, taking advantage of the barbarians' lack of caution, loosed his troops in a surprise attack and killed or wounded many.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians sent General Murong Baiyao with a great host to aid them. Wenxiu already held the court's commission and, catching the barbarians off guard, loosed a surprise attack that killed and wounded many.

sentences.zh: 虜乃進軍圍城，文秀善於撫御，將士咸為盡力，每與虜戰，輒摧破之，掩擊營寨，往無不捷。

translations.literal: The barbarians then advanced and besieged the city. Wenxiu was skilled at winning men; officers and soldiers all fought with their utmost. Each battle with the barbarians broke them; raids on their camps never failed.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians then advanced and besieged the city. Wenxiu knew how to win men's hearts; officers and soldiers fought their hardest. Every clash broke the barbarians; every raid on their camps succeeded.

sentences.zh: 太宗進文秀號輔國將軍。

translations.literal: The Taizong advanced Wenxiu to General Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming advanced Wenxiu to General Who Assists the State.

sentences.zh: 其年八月，虜蜀郡公拔式等馬步數萬人入西郭，直至城下。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of that year the barbarian Duke of Shu Jun Ba Shi and others led several tens of thousands of horse and foot into the western suburb as far as the foot of the wall.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of that year the barbarian Duke of Shu Jun Ba Shi and others led tens of thousands of horse and foot into the western suburb right to the foot of the wall.

sentences.zh: 文秀使輔國將軍垣諶擊破之。

translations.literal: Wenxiu sent General Who Assists the State Yuan Shen to defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu sent Yuan Shen, General Who Assists the State, to defeat them.

sentences.zh: 九月，又逼城東。

translations.literal: In the ninth month they pressed the eastern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month they pressed the east wall.

sentences.zh: 十月，進攻南郭。

translations.literal: In the tenth month they attacked the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month they assaulted the south wall.

sentences.zh: 文秀使員外散騎侍郎黃彌之等邀擊，斬獲數千。

translations.literal: Wenxiu sent Supernumerary Gentleman-at-Large Huang Mizhi and others to intercept them and beheaded or captured several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu sent Huang Mizhi, Supernumerary Gentleman-at-Large, and others to intercept them and killed or captured several thousand.

sentences.zh: 四年，又進文秀號右將軍，封新城縣侯，食邑五百戶。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Wenxiu was again advanced to General of the Right Army and enfeoffed as Marquis of Xincheng with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Wenxiu was promoted to General of the Right Army and enfeoffed as Marquis of Xincheng with five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 虜青州刺史王隆顯於安丘縣又為軍主高崇仁所破，死者數百人。

translations.literal: The barbarian Qingzhou Inspector Wang Longxian was again defeated at Anqiu by Commander Gao Chongren; several hundred died.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarian Qingzhou Inspector Wang Longxian was again beaten at Anqiu by Commander Gao Chongren; several hundred perished.

sentences.zh: 虜圍青州積久，太宗所遣救兵並不敢進，乃以文秀弟征北中兵參軍文靜為輔國將軍，統高密、北海、平昌、長廣、東萊五郡軍事，從海道救青州。

translations.literal: The barbarians had besieged Qingzhou a long time and the relief armies the Taizong sent dared not advance; he therefore made Wenxiu's younger brother Northern Campaign Aide Wen Jing General Who Assists the State, commanding military affairs in five commanderies, to rescue Qingzhou by sea.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians had besieged Qingzhou a long time and the relief armies Emperor Ming sent dared not advance; he therefore made Wenxiu's younger brother Northern Campaign Aide Wen Jing General Who Assists the State, commanding military affairs in five commanderies, to rescue Qingzhou by sea.

sentences.zh: 文靜至東萊之不其城，為虜所斷遏，不得進，因保城自守，又為虜所攻，屢戰輒克，太宗加其東青州刺史。

translations.literal: Jing reached Buji in Donglai but was blocked by the barbarians and could not advance; he therefore held the city and defended himself, was again attacked by the barbarians, yet won battle after battle; the Taizong added the title Eastern Qingzhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Jing reached Buji in Donglai but was blocked by the barbarians and could not advance; he therefore held the city and defended himself, was again attacked by the barbarians, yet won battle after battle; Emperor Ming added the title Eastern Qingzhou Inspector.

sentences.zh: 四年，不其城為虜所陷，文靜見殺。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Buji fell to the barbarians and Jing was killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Buji fell and Jing was killed.

sentences.zh: 文秀被圍三載，外無援軍，士卒為之用命，無離叛者，日夜戰鬥，甲胄生蟣虱。

translations.literal: Wenxiu was besieged three years with no relief from outside; his soldiers served him faithfully and none deserted. They fought day and night until lice bred in their armour.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu was besieged three years without relief; his men stayed loyal and none deserted. They fought day and night until lice swarmed in their armour.

sentences.zh: 五年正月二十四日，遂為虜所陷。

translations.literal: On the twenty-fourth day of the first month of the fifth year the city at last fell to the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-fourth day of the first month of the fifth year the city finally fell to the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 城敗之日，解釋戎衣，緩服靜坐，命左右取所持節。

translations.literal: On the day the city fell he removed his armour, put on loose garments, and sat quietly, ordering his attendants to fetch the staff of office he held.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he took off his armour, put on plain clothes, and sat quietly, telling his attendants to bring the staff of office he carried.

sentences.zh: 虜既入，兵刃交至，問曰：「青州刺史沈文秀何在？

translations.literal: Once the barbarians had entered, weapons crossed before him and they asked, "Where is Qingzhou Inspector Shen Wenxiu?"
translations.idiomatic: Once the barbarians were inside, weapons flashed before him and they cried, "Where is Qingzhou Inspector Shen Wenxiu?"

sentences.zh: 」文秀厲聲曰：「身是。

translations.literal: Wenxiu said loudly, "I am he."
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu called out, "It is I."

sentences.zh: 」因執之，牽出聽事前，剝取衣服。

translations.literal: He was seized and dragged out before the main hall, where his clothes were stripped off.
translations.idiomatic: They seized him and dragged him before the main hall, where they stripped off his clothes.

sentences.zh: 時白曜在城西南角樓，裸縛文秀至曜前，執之者令拜。

translations.literal: At that time Baiyao was in the tower at the southwest corner of the wall. Wenxiu was bound naked and brought before Baiyao; those holding him ordered him to bow.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao was then in the tower at the southwest corner. Wenxiu was bound naked and brought before him; his captors ordered him to bow.

sentences.zh: 文秀曰：「各二國大臣，無相拜之禮。

translations.literal: Wenxiu said, "We are ministers of two states—there is no ritual of bowing between us."
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu said, "We are ministers of two states—there is no bowing between us."

sentences.zh: 」曜命還其衣，為設酒食，鏁送桑乾。

translations.literal: Baiyao ordered his clothes returned, set out food and wine, and sent him under guard to Sanggan.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao had his clothes returned, set out food and wine, and sent him under guard to Sanggan.

sentences.zh: 其餘為亂兵所殺，死者甚眾。

translations.literal: The rest were killed by the disorderly troops; the dead were very many.
translations.idiomatic: The rest were cut down by the disorderly troops; the dead were very numerous.

sentences.zh: 太宗先遣尚書功論郎何如真選青州文武，亦為虜所殺。

translations.literal: The Taizong had earlier sent Minister of Works Reviewer He Ruzhen to select Qingzhou civil and military officers; he too was killed by the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming had earlier sent Minister of Works Reviewer He Ruzhen to select Qingzhou civil and military officers; he too was killed by the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 文秀在桑乾凡十九年，齊之永明四年，病死，時年六十一。

translations.literal: Wenxiu remained at Sanggan nineteen years in all. In the fourth year of Yongming of Qi he died of illness, aged sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu spent nineteen years at Sanggan in all. In the fourth year of Yongming of Qi he died of illness, aged sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 崔道固，清河人也。

translations.literal: Cui Daogu was a native of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Daogu was from Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 世祖世，以幹用見知，歷太子屯騎校尉，左軍將軍。

translations.literal: During the Shizu reign he was known for practical ability and served as Crown Prince Commandant of the Escort Cavalry and General of the Left Army.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Xiaowu's reign he was known for practical ability and served as Crown Prince Commandant of the Escort Cavalry and General of the Left Army.

sentences.zh: 大明三年，出為齊、北海二郡太守。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daming he went out as Governor of Qi and Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Daming he was sent out as Governor of Qi and Beihai.

sentences.zh: 民焦恭破古塚，得玉鎧，道固檢得，獻之，執繫恭。

translations.literal: The commoner Jiao Gong broke open an ancient tomb and obtained a jade suit of armour; Daogu seized it on inspection, presented it to the throne, and had Gong arrested.
translations.idiomatic: A commoner named Jiao Gong broke open an ancient tomb and found a jade suit of armour; Daogu seized it on inspection, presented it to the throne, and arrested Gong.

sentences.zh: 入為新安王子鸞北中郎諮議參軍，永嘉王子仁左軍司馬。

translations.literal: He entered court as Consultant to the Northern Gentlemen of the Prince of Xin'an Ziluan and as Left Army Marshal to the Prince of Yongjia Ziren.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Consultant to the Northern Gentlemen of Prince Ziluan of Xin'an and as Left Army Marshal to Prince Ziren of Yongjia.

sentences.zh: 景和元年，出為寧朔將軍、冀州刺史，鎮歷城。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jinghe he went out as General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Jizhou, stationed at Licheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jinghe he was sent out as General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Jizhou, with his seat at Licheng.

sentences.zh: 泰始二年，進號輔國將軍，又進號征虜將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taishi he was advanced to General Who Assists the State and again to General Who Subdues the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taishi he was promoted to General Who Assists the State and then again to General Who Subdues the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 時徐州刺史薛安都同逆，上即還道固本號為徐州代之。

translations.literal: At that time Xuzhou Inspector Xue Andou had joined the rebellion; the court at once returned Daogu to his original rank and made him Inspector of Xuzhou in Andou's place.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xuzhou Inspector Xue Andou had joined the rebellion; the court at once restored Daogu to his former rank and made him Inspector of Xuzhou in Andou's place.

sentences.zh: 道固不受命，遣子景微、軍主傅靈越率眾赴安都。

translations.literal: Daogu did not accept the commission and sent his son Jingwei and Commander Fu Lingyue with troops to join Andou.
translations.idiomatic: Daogu refused the commission and sent his son Jingwei and Commander Fu Lingyue with troops to support Andou.

sentences.zh: 既而為土人起義所攻，屢戰失利，閉門自守。

translations.literal: He was then attacked by local loyalist uprisings, lost battle after battle, and shut the gates to defend himself.
translations.idiomatic: He was then attacked by local loyalist forces, suffered defeat after defeat, and shut the gates to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 會四方平定，上遣使宣慰，道固奉詔歸順。

translations.literal: When the four quarters were pacified the court sent envoys to comfort him and Daogu accepted the edict and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When the four quarters were pacified the court sent envoys to reassure him, and Daogu accepted the edict and submitted.

sentences.zh: 先是與沈文秀共引虜，虜既至，固守距之，因被圍逼。

translations.literal: Earlier he had together with Shen Wenxiu invited the barbarians; when they arrived he held firm and resisted them and was thus besieged.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier he and Shen Wenxiu had together invited the barbarians; when they arrived he held firm and resisted them and was besieged.

sentences.zh: 虜每進，輒為道固所摧。

translations.literal: Each time the barbarians advanced they were broken by Daogu.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the barbarians advanced they were beaten back by Daogu.

sentences.zh: 三年，以為都督冀、青、兗、幽、并五州諸軍事、前將軍、冀州刺史，加節，又進號平北將軍。

translations.literal: In the third year he was made Commander over military affairs in the five prefectures Ji, Qing, Yan, You, and Bing, Former General, and Inspector of Jizhou with staff of authority, and again advanced to General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made Commander over military affairs in Ji, Qing, Yan, You, and Bing, Former General, and Inspector of Jizhou with staff of authority, and was again advanced to General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 其年，為虜所陷，被送桑乾，死於虜中。

translations.literal: That year he was taken by the barbarians, sent to Sanggan, and died among them.
translations.idiomatic: That year the city fell to the barbarians; he was sent to Sanggan and died in captivity.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：《春秋》列國大夫得罪，皆先致其邑而後去，唯邾、莒三臣，書以叛人之目，蓋重地也。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: In the Spring and Autumn Annals, when great officers of the feudal states offended, all first surrendered their fiefs before departing—only the three ministers of Zhu and Ju are recorded under the heading of rebels, because territory weighed heavily.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: In the Spring and Autumn Annals, when great officers of the feudal states fell into disgrace, all first surrendered their fiefs before leaving—only the three ministers of Zhu and Ju are entered as rebels, because territory was held in the highest regard.

sentences.zh: 安都勤王之略，義闕於藩屏，以地外奔，罪同於三叛。

translations.literal: Andou's plan to aid the sovereign lacked righteousness as a screen for the realm; fleeing abroad with his territory, his crime was the same as the three rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Andou's scheme to aid the sovereign fell short of the duty owed a frontier shield; fleeing beyond the borders with his territory, his crime matched that of the three rebels.

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：「誰生厲階，至今為梗。

translations.literal: The Odes say: "Who raised this grievous stair? To this day it remains a stumbling block."
translations.idiomatic: As the Odes have it: "Who raised this grievous stair? Even now it remains a stumbling block."

sentences.zh: 」其此之謂乎？

translations.literal: Is this not what is meant?
translations.idiomatic: Is this not what those words describe?
